title.zh: Crusoe将怀俄明州问题数据中心项目出售给谷歌，后者计划投资170亿美元接手开发
title.en: Crusoe Sells Troubled Wyoming Data Center Project to Google, Which Plans $17 Billion Investment to Take Over Development

current_state.zh:
11月7日，AI数据中心开发商Crusoe确认将其位于美国怀俄明州东南部的一处未完工数据中心项目出售给谷歌。谷歌计划投资170亿美元接手并继续开发，但双方未披露具体收购价格。

此次交易标志着顶级AI实验室从潜在客户角色转向直接所有权，以规避建设成本和工期风险。这凸显了独立开发商在交付大规模AI基础设施方面面临的系统性挑战。

该项目最初由Crusoe与获得黑石支持的基础设施公司Tallgrass于2025年公布，规划最终将电力容量扩大至10吉瓦。此前，谷歌曾考虑成为该项目客户，但因担忧Crusoe管理下的建设成本及工期问题，最终决定接管项目。
current_state.en:
On November 7, AI data center developer Crusoe confirmed the sale of its unfinished 10GW data center project in southeastern Wyoming to Google. Google plans to invest $17 billion to take over and continue the development, though the specific acquisition price was not disclosed.

This transaction marks a strategic shift where a top-tier AI lab moves from a potential customer role to direct ownership to mitigate construction cost and timeline risks. It highlights the systemic challenges independent developers face in delivering massive-scale AI infrastructure.

The project was originally announced in 2025 by Crusoe and Blackstone-backed Tallgrass, with a target capacity of 10 gigawatts. Google previously considered being a customer but decided to take over due to concerns about management under Crusoe.

updates.background_zh: Crusoe Energy Systems的商业模式是与石油和天然气公司合作，利用废弃的天然气为AI基础设施供电。10吉瓦的规模代表了工业级体量，相当于为数十万户家庭供电，这在其他主要AI基础设施计划中也是一种趋势。
updates.background_en: Crusoe Energy Systems operates a business model that partners with oil and gas companies to utilize wasted natural gas for AI infrastructure. The 10GW scale represents an industrial magnitude comparable to powering hundreds of thousands of homes, a trend seen in other major AI infrastructure plans.
updates.market_impact_zh: 该交易表明对大规模电力基础设施的需求增加，可能会影响与数据中心开发相关的AI基础设施股票和能源资产的情绪。它强调了下一代计算能力所需的资本密集度。
updates.market_impact_en: The deal signals increased demand for large-scale power infrastructure and may influence sentiment around AI infrastructure stocks and energy assets tied to data center development. It underscores the capital intensity required for next-generation compute capacity.
